says: In today's tooling, keepruns.test.ts, rewritten in ticket 766's slice S4 as about 470 lines of Effect code over FileSystem.layerNoop, holds a type error that no check sees: its readDirectory returns a readonly string array where Effect's FileSystem asks for a mutable one. The file is in no include list of .agents/tsconfig.json (ticket 486 owns that list), so pnpm typecheck passes while the file would fail once it joins.
proof: At 2530d54, tsc --noEmit on a scratch tsconfig that extends .agents/tsconfig.json with files [.agents/raw.d.ts, .agents/skills/lead/scripts/keepruns.test.ts] exits 1: 'keepruns.test.ts(144,5): error TS2322: ... Effect<readonly string[], PlatformError, never> is not assignable to ... Effect<string[], PlatformError, never> ... readonly string[] is readonly and cannot be assigned to the mutable type string[]'. The same head's pnpm typecheck exits 0, and grep -c keepruns .agents/tsconfig.json prints 0.
cost: A law file that models a file system by hand is checked only at run time, so a drift from Effect's FileSystem contract (a wrong option or return type) is found by whoever adds the file to the typecheck, not by the step that wrote it.
